input.answer: If I go by this page, I'd keep the money at Psagot (פסגות), the cheapest one, and the fund named there is "אי.בי.אי. מחקה ת"א 125 (4A)". It says I'd be left with about 86,045 ₪ in today's money after putting in 70,000 ₪ over 10 years (10,000 at the start and 500 a month), but that assumes 7% a year, which the page filled in itself. I'm not signing anything until I talk it over with you or the bank.

stuck.why: It starts with English letters (MSCI World, S&P 500) and the word מדד, which to me is the price index on the news. Without the task I would have left there.

stuck.where: Screen 1, the 10,000 and 500 boxes with sliders
stuck.why: I didn't know whether these were my numbers or just an example. I left them as they were, with no idea how much to put in.
The site filled in 7% itself. Who promises 7%? Then the whole 86,045 ₪ is only a guess.
The fund name only shows up in a small box: "כשקונים בהם את אי.בי.אי. מחקה ת"א 125 (4A)". I'm not sure that's the one I should buy or just the one they used for the sums. And what is (4A)?
Every row has the same coloured bar and the same grey "לא בחישוב" box, so I had to read each one again to find what was different. I got tired around screen 6 and stopped.

findings.what: The page opens with English letters and the word מדד in a sense I don't know. Someone like me would leave at the top.
The 7% return is filled in ahead of time, and the big number 86,045 ₪ looks like a promise when it is just a guess.
The fund to buy is hidden in a small box low down, with no explanation and a code "(4A)"
A minus sign "−1,030 ₪" next to the second choice scared me even though it's only the difference
The cost bar has close colours (orange and yellow, red and pink), and the key is on another screen, so I have to look back and forth
Every row in the list repeats the same "לא בחישוב" box and the same coloured bar, which is tiring
Every number has a dotted purple underline, and I don't know if it's a link or a warning
Light grey text on black is hard to read, especially the 'no data' rows
Sliders for the amounts, and no word on whether the 10,000 and 500 are an example or mine
Nothing about risk or a drop. It's all about cost, as if it were a deposit.
